cards.name: 3D Rotate
cards.summary: Turns an image in 3D as if it were a flat card swung on its vertical and horizontal axes, so it renders in perspective: one edge recedes and shrinks, the opposite edge comes forward. Best fit scales the turned image back inside the original frame. It tilts a flat plane only, with no depth or sides.
use_for: tilting a screenshot or photo panel for a device or web mock-up
angled photo cards in a collage, brochure or event poster
a quick perspective lean on a picture without building a 3D scene
avoid: vector artwork that must stay crisp and editable: use Object/Perspective/Add Perspective on the vectors instead
angles near the -75 / 75 limit squash the image to a sliver and soften it through resampling; stay within about 45
a solid 3D object with visible sides: this only tilts a plane, use Effects/Extrude on vector shapes
the scripted path works on bitmaps only (Shape.Bitmap): run Object/Convert to Bitmap on vector art first
scripts: this effect's command string has not been apply-tested (format proven on other effects); check the result

scripts: the 2026-10-13 gallery render found no working scripted call (RuntimeError: ApplyBitmapEffect changed no pixel of the plate (or raised RPC_E_SERVERFAULT) for every form tried: 'ThreeDRotateEffect [...]); apply it from the menu, dialog or docker

params.name: VertAngle
params.does: Vertical rotation angle in degrees (-75 to 75, default 0, step 1): turns the image about one axis so one pair of opposite edges recedes in perspective. Which axis, and which sign sends which edge back, is not in the harvest: check the preview

params.name: HorizAngle
params.does: Horizontal rotation angle in degrees (-75 to 75, default 0, step 1): turns the image about the other axis. Which axis, and which sign sends which edge back, is not in the harvest: check the preview

params.name: BestFit
params.does: On: scales the turned image to fit inside the original object's bounds. Off: keeps the original scale

pairs_with: Drop Shadow (grounds the tilted panel on the page)
Object/Convert to Bitmap (gives vector art a bitmap for the scripted path)
cards.scripting: shape.Bitmap.ApplyBitmapEffect("PGD 3D Rotate", "ThreeDRotateEffect VertAngle=20,HorizAngle=40,BestFit=1")  // shape must be a bitmap; command format proven on 6 other effects but this string not apply-tested, and the bool spelling (1 / true) is unproven. Menu route: FrameWork InvokeItem 11f14b2e-099d-4871-aced-bc9be70b9581 (opens the dialog)
cards.non_destructive: yes from the Effects menu: CorelDRAW 2024 keeps it in the object's effect stack (editable, removable). The harvest does not say whether the scripted Bitmap.ApplyBitmapEffect result stays editable.
cards.cost: light: one perspective resample of the bitmap

review.changes: VertAngle / HorizAngle descriptions no longer assert which axis each angle turns around (not in the harvest); range, default and step stated from the batch

verified.note: No frame: failed.json says "RuntimeError: ApplyBitmapEffect changed no pixel of the plate (or raised RPC_E_SERVERFAULT) for every form tried: 'ThreeDRotateEffect VertAngle=20,HorizAngle=40,BestFit=1'"; VertAngle 20 / HorizAngle 40 are far from the 0 no-op, so the demo is not the cause; harness, not the effect: no working scripted route was found, so the effect itself is untested; status set to needs_input.

second_opinion.note: Harness check: no frame exists, failed.json names the scripted route (every command form tried), not the effect, so 'broken' here means the render broke; the card text hedges the script route and makes no look claim from a frame. Every listed form (and the object-model twin where one exists) changed nothing, and the demo values are far from a no-op, so needs_input is the honest status, matching Selective Color / Tone Curve.

cards.name: Cylinder
cards.summary: Remaps the image as if it were wrapped round a cylinder, along one direction only: positive Percentage stretches the middle and crowds the ends, negative does the reverse. With Mode sent as list index 0 (Horizontal in the harvested list order; the caption form changed no pixel) the remap runs down the height: on the 2026-10 gallery render (Percentage 100) the middle rows were stretched taller and the top and bottom rows crowded (the colour strip was squeezed from 45 to 27 px against the bottom edge) while every column kept its width, so Horizontal is a cylinder lying on its side; Vertical presumably works across the width, the upright can (not rendered). It only moves pixels: no shading, no perspective.
use_for: previewing a label wrapped round a cylinder lying on its side (Horizontal) or an upright can, bottle or tube (Vertical, inferred from the Horizontal render)
stretching the middle band of a photo strip or banner while crowding its ends, along one axis only
one-axis bulge on a picture where a full sphere distortion would be too much
avoid: a round bulge in both directions: use Effects/3D Effects/Sphere
a realistic product render with shading: this only remaps pixels, add a highlight / shadow gradient on top
vector art to keep editable: envelope the vectors with Effects/Envelope instead
the scripted path works on bitmaps only: run Object/Convert to Bitmap first; this effect's command string has not been apply-tested

params.name: Percentage
params.does: Strength and sign of the wrap (-100 to 100): positive stretches the middle outward, negative pinches it in

params.name: Mode
params.does: Axis of the remap: on the render Horizontal (sent as list index 0; the caption 'Horizontal' changed no pixel) remapped the rows and left the column widths alone, a cylinder lying on its side; Vertical presumably remaps the columns (an upright can)
params.typical: Vertical for an upright can label read left to right (inferred), Horizontal for a lying cylinder

pairs_with: Effects/3D Effects/Sphere (round bulge instead of one-axis)
Transparency gradient over the bitmap to fake cylindrical shading
cards.scripting: shape.Bitmap.ApplyBitmapEffect("PGD Cylinder", "CylinderEffect Percentage=100,Mode=0") (the form the render test used: enum keys go as their list index, captions are ignored: Mode 0 Horizontal, 1 Vertical)  // shape must be a bitmap; ImageNode (unlabelled list in the template) left out; command format proven on 6 other effects but this string not apply-tested. Menu route: FrameWork InvokeItem bf319b1a-09c2-403b-9531-ba1cf09c1059
cards.non_destructive: yes from the Effects menu: CorelDRAW 2024 keeps it in the object's effect stack. The harvest does not say whether the scripted result stays editable.

review.changes: summary, look and use_for no longer claim straight lines bow / barrel distortion (a one-axis remap changes spacing, it does not curve lines); Mode description made consistent (it was both 'direction of the distortion' and 'the cylinder's orientation', which are opposite axes)

verified.note: A one-axis wrap did happen, but along the height: with Mode Horizontal (sent as list index 0) the middle rows are stretched taller and the top and bottom rows crowded (the colour strip squeezed from 45 to 27 px against the bottom edge) while every column keeps its width, so Horizontal is a cylinder lying on its side, not the upright can the card described; summary, use_for and the Mode note rewritten.

second_opinion.note: Re-measured: the colour strip's red swatch runs y 483-509 (ref 440-484) while the blue swatch keeps x 600-719, so rows were remapped and columns kept. Harness check: Mode went as list index 0 because the caption 'Horizontal' changed no pixel, and index 0 = Horizontal is the harvested list order, not proven; the rewrite therefore states the axis for the value sent and hedges Vertical as inferred.

cards.name: Emboss
cards.summary: Turns the image into a raised relief: flat areas become a single tone and every edge is drawn as a light ridge on one side and a dark ridge on the other, as if stamped into metal or paper and lit from the Direction angle. Color mode sets the base tone: the original colours, gray, black, or a chosen colour.
use_for: stamped metal, embossed paper or coin-like texture from a photo or logo bitmap
a subtle relief background texture behind type (lower the opacity)
turning a busy photo into a monochrome relief for a poster backdrop
avoid: soft or low-contrast images give a weak, mushy relief: raise Depth and Level, or sharpen first
a bevel on vector type or shapes: use Effects/Bevel, which keeps the vectors
keeping the photo readable: Gray / Black flatten all colour; use Original color mode or a transparency over the source

params.name: Depth
params.does: Height of the relief, i.e. how wide and strong the edge ridges are (1 to 20)

params.name: Level
params.does: Contrast / intensity of the highlight and shadow ridges (1 to 500, log slider)

params.name: Direction
params.does: Light direction in degrees (0 to 360): which side of each edge gets the highlight

params.name: ColorMode
params.does: Base tone of the flat areas: Original color, Gray, Black, or Other (uses ColorItem)

params.name: ColorItem
params.does: The custom base colour used when ColorMode is Other

pairs_with: Transparency over the embossed copy to blend relief with the original photo
Effects/Bevel (vector bevel for type set over the relief)
cards.scripting: shape.Bitmap.ApplyBitmapEffect("PGD Emboss", "EmbossEffect Depth=8,Level=250,Direction=135,ColorMode=1") (the form the render test used: enum keys go as their list index, captions are ignored: ColorMode 0 Original color, 1 Gray, 2 Black, 3 Other)  // shape must be a bitmap; ColorItem is not in the command template, so ColorMode=Other from a script uses whatever colour the effect already holds. Menu route: FrameWork InvokeItem 09ea28c1-bf15-49c5-85d6-7a5037ee5cd1
cards.non_destructive: yes from the Effects menu: CorelDRAW 2024 keeps it in the object's effect stack. The harvest does not say whether the scripted result stays editable.

review.changes: scripting note: ColorMode=Other cannot get its colour from a script (ColorItem not in the template); everything else checked against the batch and the apply test

verified.note: The plate became a flat mid-grey relief: every edge (radial lines, mid-tone detail, stripes, panel rims, type) is drawn as a light ridge on one side and a dark ridge on the other, lit from the upper left; the swatch borders keep thin coloured lines, everything else is grey (ColorMode Gray, sent as index 1).

cards.name: Page Curl
cards.summary: Peels one corner of the image back like a turning page: the chosen corner rolls over, the back of the curl is drawn in the Curl colour (or lets the image show through when Paper is Transparent), and the uncovered area takes the Background colour. Width and Height set how far the curl reaches; the harvest could not read their defaults.
use_for: a 'turn the page' corner on a brochure, flyer or e-book cover mock-up
a retro sticker / peel-off corner on a photo
hinting there is more content behind a picture in a promo layout
avoid: modern flat layouts: the effect reads as dated clip-art; a soft drop shadow under a folded vector corner looks cleaner
scripts that need the Curl / Background colours: PaintColorItem and BackColorItem are not in the command template, so a script cannot set them and gets the effect's current colours (not read)
the scripted path works on bitmaps only, and this effect's command string has not been apply-tested; its live defaults and bound ranges were not read

params.name: CornerType
params.does: Which corner peels: CornerNW (top-left), CornerNE (top-right), CornerSW (bottom-left), CornerSE (bottom-right)

params.name: DirectionType
params.does: Whether the curl rolls along the vertical or the horizontal direction

params.name: PaperType
params.does: Opaque draws the back of the curl in the Curl colour; Transparent lets the image show through it

params.name: Curl
params.does: Colour of the curled-over back of the page

params.name: Background
params.does: Colour of the area uncovered behind the curl

params.name: Width
params.does: Size of the curl along the image width (1 to 100; the harvest gives no unit and no default; exact meaning not render-checked)

params.name: Height
params.does: Size of the curl along the image height (1 to 100; the harvest gives no unit and no default; exact meaning not render-checked)

pairs_with: Drop Shadow (under the bitmap so the peeled page lifts off the layout)
cards.scripting: shape.Bitmap.ApplyBitmapEffect("PGD Page Curl", "PageCurlEffect CornerType=CornerSE,DirectionType=Vertical,PaperType=Opaque,Width=55,Height=65")  // shape must be a bitmap; colours (PaintColorItem, BackColorItem) not settable through the template; command format proven on 6 other effects but this string not apply-tested. Menu route: FrameWork InvokeItem 0902e8d0-83bf-4cd7-8191-9fc0cca2a9d0
cards.non_destructive: yes from the Effects menu: CorelDRAW 2024 keeps it in the object's effect stack. The harvest does not say whether the scripted result stays editable.

review.changes: Width / Height descriptions mark unit, default and exact meaning as unharvested; colour avoid line no longer claims what the data source holds (it was never read)

verified.note: The bottom-right corner (CornerSE) is peeled up and back in a vertical curl: the back of the curl is a silver-grey gradient and the uncovered corner is plain white, the turning-page look described.

cards.name: Pinch/Punch
cards.summary: Distorts the image around its centre: pinch draws the middle in so it looks sucked away from the viewer, punch pushes it out so it bulges toward the viewer, with straight lines bending into curves around the centre. One slider from -100 to 100 sets direction and strength; check which sign gives which on the preview.
use_for: a funhouse / caricature bulge or pinch on a face or product shot
a pull toward the centre (no twist) for a dramatic poster backdrop
making a product or icon in the middle of a bitmap swell slightly toward the viewer
avoid: text and logos in the middle of the image get badly warped; keep them on a separate object
a clean spherical lens bulge: Effects/3D Effects/Sphere gives a rounder, lens-like result
the scripted path works on bitmaps only, and this effect's command string has not been apply-tested
a spiral / twisting pull: this only pushes or pulls radially, use Effects/Distort/Swirl or Whirlpool

params.name: PinchPunch
params.does: Direction and strength of the distortion (-100 to 100); one sign pinches the centre in, the other punches it out, 0 is no change

pairs_with: Effects/3D Effects/Sphere (stacked for a stronger lens bulge)
cards.scripting: shape.Bitmap.ApplyBitmapEffect("PGD Pinch/Punch", "PinchPunchEffect PinchPunch=-100")  // shape must be a bitmap; ImageNode (unlabelled list) left out; command format proven on 6 other effects but this string not apply-tested. Menu route: FrameWork InvokeItem 214c1838-0b59-4f33-88f7-062d438bd558
cards.non_destructive: yes from the Effects menu: CorelDRAW 2024 keeps it in the object's effect stack. The harvest does not say whether the scripted result stays editable.

review.changes: demo_settings and scripting 100 -> -100 (100 is the harvested default, so a demo at it cannot prove the command string was read; -100 is the other full-strength side); removed 'vortex' (pinch has no twist; Swirl / Whirlpool added to avoid) and the self-contradictory 'punch to reduce barrel-like pinching' use

verified.note: Strong centre distortion: at -100 the middle of the plate swells toward the viewer (the wall at the centre becomes a huge arch, the large shapes either side are pushed outward and lean, the colour strip bows downward in the middle), so on this render the negative sign gave the bulge.

cards.name: Sphere
cards.summary: Wraps the image onto a sphere: the centre swells outward (positive Percentage) or caves in (negative) in both directions at once, like looking through a fisheye lens or a glass ball, with lines bowing around the middle. Optimize trades render speed for smoother quality.
use_for: fisheye / glass-ball look on a photo for a poster or social graphic
a bubble or globe feel on a circular badge image
a convex 'magnified' centre to draw attention to the middle of a picture
avoid: a bulge along one axis only: use Effects/3D Effects/Cylinder
faces near the centre get swollen at high values; keep it under about 50 for people
the scripted path works on bitmaps only, and this effect's command string has not been apply-tested

params.name: Percentage
params.does: Strength and sign of the sphere (-100 to 100): positive bulges the centre out, negative caves it in

params.name: Optimize
params.does: Speed renders faster; Quality gives smoother interpolation

pairs_with: Effects/3D Effects/Pinch/Punch (stack for a stronger bulge)
an elliptical PowerClip or crop to a circle for a globe badge

cards.cost: light; Quality is slower than Speed on large bitmaps

cards.name: Zig Zag
cards.summary: Bends the image with waves radiating from its centre: Pond Ripples gives concentric rings like a stone dropped in water, Out from center pushes the waves outward along radial lines, Around center twists them in rotating swirls. Waves sets how many rings, Strength how far pixels move, Damping how quickly the waves die away.
use_for: water-ripple or reflection look on a photo or poster backdrop
a hypnotic / psychedelic swirl background for party or music flyers
a 'shockwave' distortion behind a headline
avoid: straight parallel waves across the image: use Effects/Distort/Ripple
readable text or faces near the centre: they break up even at moderate Strength
the scripted path works on bitmaps only, and this effect's command string has not been apply-tested

params.name: WaveType
params.does: Wave pattern: id_ripples (Pond Ripples), id_out (Out from center), id_around (Around center)

params.name: Waves
params.does: Number of waves (1 to 100): rings for Pond Ripples / Out from center, swirl bands for Around center

params.name: Strength
params.does: How far pixels are displaced (-100 to 100); the sign flips the wave phase

params.name: Damping
params.does: How quickly the waves fade away across the image (1 to 100)

params.name: WaveOptimization
params.does: id_speed renders faster; id_quality interpolates more smoothly

pairs_with: a blue / teal colour adjustment for a water look
